rationale: The answer covers much of the core Rule 6c-11 framework. It correctly says the website must be free and public. It says prior-day portfolio holdings must be posted before market open each business day and distinguishes them from creation/redemption baskets. It includes daily NAV, market price and premium/discount, and gives the correct history period (last calendar year plus completed quarters). It also includes the 30-calendar-day median bid-ask spread and the >2% for more than seven consecutive trading days trigger. However, it has a material localized error: it says the sustained-deviation explanation stays posted only until the deviation no longer exceeds 2%. The rule requires it to remain on the website for at least one year. It also says 'a table or chart' when both a table and a line graph are required. It omits the 'or shorter fund life' qualifier for the history period. It omits the holdings detail (identifiers, descriptions, quantities, weights) and the spread methodology (NBBO at 10-second intervals, midpoint normalization, percentage rounded to a hundredth). The core is useful, but the retention-period error and these omissions keep it from being correct.
